rates.title: Rates
rates.why_it_matters: Rising real yields compress equity multiples and signal tighter financial conditions.

sections.question: Is the move in yields demand-driven or inflation-driven?
sections.answer: The current rise in nominal 10Y is predominantly real-yield driven, not breakeven-driven, consistent with demand-led tightening rather than an inflation-expectations shock.
sections.why: Real-yield-driven moves compress equity multiples more directly than breakeven-driven moves, which can be partially offset by pricing power.
sections.risk: If real yields reach 2.5%, historical precedent suggests meaningful equity multiple compression.
sections.support: Breakeven inflation is anchored below 2.5%, limiting stagflation framing.
sections.caveat: NY Fed ACM term premium data is unavailable; duration risk decomposition is incomplete.
